question: Can you score straight from a throw-in?
expected_answer: No. If the ball enters the opponents' goal directly a goal kick is awarded; if it enters the thrower's own goal a corner kick is awarded.

question: Can you be offside from a corner?
expected_answer: No. There is no offside offence if a player receives the ball directly from a corner kick (nor from a goal kick or a throw-in).

question: How big is a football?
expected_answer: A circumference of 68-70 cm (27-28 ins) and a weight of 410-450 g (14-16 oz) at the start of the match.

question: How far back does the wall have to be at a free kick?
expected_answer: At least 9.15 m (10 yds) from the ball until it is in play.

question: Who picks ends at the start of the game?
expected_answer: The referee tosses a coin; the team that wins the toss decides which goal to attack in the first half or to take the kick-off.

question: Can the keeper pick up a back-pass?
expected_answer: No. If the goalkeeper handles the ball after it has been deliberately kicked to them by a team-mate an indirect free kick is awarded.

question: Can a keeper score with a goal kick?
expected_answer: Yes; a goal may be scored directly from a goal kick but only against the opposing team. If it goes directly into the kicker's own goal a corner kick is awarded.

question: Is a stutter in the run-up allowed when taking a pen?
expected_answer: Feinting during the run-up is allowed. Feinting to kick once the run-up is completed is an offence: indirect free kick and the kicker is cautioned.

question: Do you get a yellow for taking your shirt off when you score?
expected_answer: Yes. Removing the shirt or covering the head with the shirt is a caution for unsporting behaviour.

question: What colour do cycling shorts under your kit have to be?
expected_answer: Undershorts/tights must be the same colour as the main colour of the shorts or the lowest part of the shorts; players of the same team must wear the same colour.

question: Can players wear jewellery now?
expected_answer: Accessories are permitted as long as they are not dangerous and are safely and securely covered. Circular 32 notes these were previously called 'jewellery'.
notes: DRAFT: vocabulary change in the 2026/27 Laws

question: How many subs can teams use in a league match?
expected_answer: Competitions may allow up to a maximum of five substitutes in official competitions (youth football is set by the national association/confederation/FIFA). The exact number is set by competition rules.

question: If extra time is needed how long is it?
expected_answer: Two equal periods not exceeding 15 minutes each; only when competition rules require a winner. A short drinks break (max one minute) is permitted at the interval of half-time in extra time.

question: What's the punishment for spitting at someone?
expected_answer: A direct free kick (or penalty) and a sending-off; spitting at someone on the team lists or a match official is a direct free kick offence and a sending-off offence.

question: After a dropped ball who gets the ball?
expected_answer: It is dropped for one player of the team that would have retained or gained possession if the referee can determine it; otherwise for one player of the team that last touched it. In the penalty area it is dropped for the defending goalkeeper.

question: How many substitues can be used in an international friendly?
expected_answer: Eight; up to eleven if both teams agree and inform the referee before the match; three substitution opportunities.
